messages:
maya: FYI — we're seeing a burst of 429s hitting per-key throttles for /v1/generate from eu-west-1 starting ~08:03 UTC. CS flagged 6 tickets. Anyone on rotation?

oliver: I'm on it. Can you paste the alert id? also which quota (per-key vs per-org) is tripping?

maya: incidents-bot posted this: <alert:ALRT-7892> '429 spike: per_key_rate_limit exceeded'

incidents-bot: ALERT ALRT-7892 triggered at 2026-03-18T08:03:12Z — metric: requests.429.rate per_key.slo=1m avg > 80pct baseline

nina: Quick sanity checks: 1) is there a rollout or traffic shift? 2) did routing policy fall back to lower-cost variant causing more tokens? 3) any known customer experiments?

ben: No rollouts in the last 24h. I see a small routing failover to uk nodes around 08:01 (health check flapping). That increased request fanout for a minute while the router retried to other pools. Logs: "router: fallback to model-v1-small for key=acme-inc due to capacity"

carla: If router retried and hit per-key limits it could create a tight feedback loop. We should temporarily raise per-key burst window or allow short burst overrides for sessions flagged as CS-urgent.

oliver: Proposed immediate actions (short checklist):
- add a temporary per-key burst allowance: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/internal/quota/override -d '{"key":"acme-inc","burst":200,"ttl":300}'`
- notify CS with ETA 15m
- create a dashboard tile for per-key 429 rate + recent routing fallbacks

maya: doing the override now for the top 3 keys in the alert. pinging CS: @cs-team — added temporary burst allowance for affected keys, monitoring.

incidents-bot: OP performed quota.override action by maya at 2026-03-18T08:05:02Z for keys [acme-inc, beta-shop, gamma-labs], burst=200 ttl=300s

nina: Mid-term: we should add an observability signal that correlates `router.fallback_rate` with `quota.per_key.429_rate` and surface it on the on-call runbook dashboard. Right now those metrics are separate and it's slow to diagnose.

ben: Agreed. For the dashboard: combine a 5m and 1m heatmap, and show top offending keys with recent policy changes. Also add an annotation layer for any quota override API calls so SRE/CS can see when manual mitigations happened.

carla: UX note for Console: make the per-key throttle override flow require a reason and auto-fill a CS ticket ID. That will help audits and avoid mystery overrides.

oliver: Longer term ideas:
- implement a short-circuit protection in the router to avoid retries that amplify 429s (exponential backoff + jitter specific to per-key errors)
- add a guard that converts repeated per-key 429s into degraded route (route away from bursty keys) rather than instant fanout

maya: Logging the action items:
- (P0) Temp burst override for top keys — done
- (P1) Dashboard tile: per-key 429 + router.fallback correlation — owner @ben — ETA EOD
- (P2) Console UX: override reason + CS ticket autofill — owner @carla — RFC next week
- (P2) Router retry/backoff changes — owner @oliver — design doc by Fri

nina: I'll update the SRE playbook entries with the exact alert id and the new checklist so CS knows the sequence to ask for on next tickets.

ben: For the dashboard query snippets, use this as starting point: ```
sum(rate(requests_total{status="429",scope="per_key"}[1m])) by (api_key)
| topk(10, sum)
```

carla: Thanks. Also add a single-click 'apply temporary burst override' button in the Console routed through ops-api with CS verification. I'll draft a mock next sprint. :+1:

maya: closing the loop here — 429s are back to baseline after the override and router stabilized. CS notified. Filing follow-up tickets for the P1/P2 items. Thanks everyone. :sparkles:
